extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and criteria for conceiving, writing, and formatting 'explainer' journalism in the Vox tradition — pieces that answer 'how' and 'why' with background, synthesis, and accessible presentation. Emphasizes topic selection, sourcing, multimedia, and specific newsroom formatting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core mission
rubrics_metrics.description: "Explain the world, add clarity, provide all the information to empower audiences, and do it in an approachable, inspiring, and helpful way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece should prioritize clarity and audience empowerment over merely reporting facts; tone should be approachable and inspiring while remaining helpful. Serve as a durable reference that makes complex topics intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic in the news but not understood
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick topics with high public attention but low public comprehension — where readers commonly ask 'Why is X happening?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target events or developments that are topical yet confusing to the public. The explainer's value is closing that comprehension gap rather than breaking a first report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background-heavy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide historical context, define terms, and map the causal chain behind events or phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include necessary context that readers need to understand current developments; avoid assuming prior knowledge. Use chronology, definitions, and causal diagrams as needed to show how things connect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evergreen + Topical
rubrics_metrics.description: Create content with a longer shelf-life than a news brief that can be updated and republished as situations evolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for reusability: explainers should serve as reference pieces that remain useful beyond immediate breaking-news cycles and can be refreshed when the topic resurfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual / multimedia integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use charts, maps, timelines, embedded video, and interactive elements to clarify complex information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals should simplify and illuminate causal links or data patterns. Prefer formats (charts, timelines, maps, interactives) that turn abstract explanations into concrete, scannable representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative source synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize authoritative sources such as researcher interviews, academic citations, and cross-referenced data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do original reporting (interviews) and cite reputable research and datasets; combine multiple sources to present a balanced, evidence-based explanation rather than relying on a single voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics suited to explainers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer topics where distance, complexity, or jargon makes understanding difficult: foreign policy, scientific discoveries, economic shifts, legal cases, cultural moments, policy debates, conflict origins, tech/AI, health/medical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this topic list as a heuristic for selecting explainer candidates — look for subjects with technical or procedural barriers to public understanding or which benefit from historical/contextual framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered subheads (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use numbered subheads to break content into clear, ordered chunks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbered subheads help readers navigate complex explanations step-by-step and support skimming; use them to structure the causal or conceptual progression of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q&A structure (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a question-and-answer framing such as 'What does this mean?' to anticipate reader questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize sections around the specific questions readers are likely to have, making the piece directly responsive and scannable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bullet point summaries (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concise bullet summaries to capture key takeaways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with or include short bullets that distill the main points for readers who want a quick understanding before diving deeper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing transparency (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about sources and how information was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly attribute facts and claims, include links to studies or primary documents, and explain journalistic methods when relevant to build trust and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What you need to know" framing (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 'What you need to know' section to foreground the essential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a brief, plain-language summary that communicates stakes and the most important facts for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Card stack format (format convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a card-stack presentation (modular blocks/cards) for discrete facts or mini-explainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modular cards allow readers to jump to subtopics and support republishing or reordering content for updates and different platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehension gap (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A demonstrable gap between what the audience knows and what the audience needs to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories where explanation meaningfully increases public understanding; absence of a gap reduces the explainer's utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear explanation of why the audience should care — the consequences or importance of the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain real-world implications and who is affected; make the relevance explicit so readers grasp the practical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern significance (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect a discrete event to a larger system or recurring pattern to show broader significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the item fits into trends, systems, or historical patterns rather than treating it as an isolated incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background dependency (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story cannot be adequately understood or told without contextual background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If understanding requires prior context, an explainer is appropriate; avoid superficial restatement of facts without necessary background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational value (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece should teach readers something substantive about systems, processes, or causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to increase readers' conceptual understanding and provide frameworks they can apply to related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusability (implicit newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Durability and potential to be updated or republished as a referent when the topic resurfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft explainers to function as evergreen resources that editors can refresh, reducing future reporting overhead and improving long-term readership value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct from news (purpose distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explainers focus on 'what it means' (background and synthesis), while news reports focus on 'what happened' (first reports of new events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to choose format and depth: breaking news demands speed and immediacy; explainers demand synthesis, context, and authoritative sourcing.
